pr_body:
* Group logging into a single debug message per (toolchain type, target platform) pair to avoid mixed output lines. This allows to reduce the length of debug lines as repeated information is explicit from the context in the previous lines.
* Use indentation to highlight resolution phases
  1. looking for all toolchains matching the target platform
  2. looking for all exec platforms matching the said toolchain
* Add a summary message containing all the selected triplets
* Less aggressive printing of exec platform resolution
* Speedup toolchain resolution a bit by stopping search as soon as all
  exec platforms have a toolchain assigned.

issue_context.title: Improve `--toolchain_resolution_debug`
issue_context.body:
The flag `--tolchain_resolution_debug` is helpful when there are problems with toolchain resolution, but is still far from perfect.

Known issues:
-  Platform mappings aren't made clear, causing confusion
-  The flag is overly verbose, while still not giving details
-  Exec groups aren't clearly grouped together

Probably more, this issue is for collecting issues and ideas.
comments: I think it would be nice if the platform being looked for was output more verbosely as well to help decipher _why_ things don't match

Outputting both the `toolchain` wrapper target and the inner `toolchain` attribute of the `toolchain` wrapper target would be really useful, I've had times where the fact that only one is output makes it hard to work out what's going on.
Reporting mismatches as "platform required X, toolchain had Y" rather than just "mismatched on cpu" would help in debuggability too.

Type @bazel_tools//tools/python:toolchain_type: target platform @local_config_platform//:host: No toolchains found.

Hi @katre , how to fix the above problem.
Closed #12110, but the suggestion to fix the ordering is a useful one.

It would be great if when a toolchain fails to resolve, the error notes the `exec` and `target` platforms/constraints that needed to be satisfied.

Currently all we get is something like (in Bazel 7 pre-release with Rules Rust configured for cross compilation);

```
(23:40:12) ERROR: lib/private/wrapper/BUILD.bazel:3:12: While resolving toolchains for target //lib/private/wrapper:hello_world: No matching toolchains found for types @rules_rust//rust:toolchain_type.
```

`--toolchain_resolution_debug` might reveal this information, but when you've got a build with several transitions on the same target it becomes very difficult to sift through all noise.

Other general suggestions I have to aid readability are;
- Cut down on repetition by revising output structure so common elements like `Type @rules_rust//rust:toolchain_type:` do not need to appear on every line.
- Keep related data (e.g. result, toolchain name, target and exec platform) aligned so comparisons can be made more easily at a glance.
- Clearly group resolution rounds (attempts to solve for a given target and/or exec platform) so the outcome can be determined.

EDIT: I restructured the output and was able to quickly spot `No toolchains found` for the target platform `//lib/private/platforms:darwin_amd64` (an easy fix in my case, discovery was the biggest issue).
